title: You’ve never seen a true crime story told quite like this 🤯  #KenRex ...
transcript: This is one of those shows that I'm like, get your tickets now before it's impossible. The show is called Ken Rex. It is playing at a tiny theatre called the Lucille Lortel Theatre off Broadway. It just won multiple Oliviers in London, and now it is having its U S. Premiere here. It is essentially a true crime podcast performed live by one guy. Well, kind of two. You have your main performer, Jack Holden, who is playing all of the characters, and you have musician John Patrick Elliott, who is providing some musical underscoring. But really, it is mainly Jack. And the way that he is able to embody all of these different characters is so impressive. He actually co wrote it with director Ed Stambollouian, and together they have crafted something that is truly tense and gripping, but also really funny at times and entertaining. There really isn't much in terms of set or props. It's really just some microphones, a staircase and a door frame. But when combined with the really incredible lighting design, some smoke, and, of course, Jack's performance, they are able to conjure up some really striking imagery. And I almost felt like I was watching a movie version of the story alongside the stage version, because the imagery that they are able to conjure up is just so vivid and such an impressive feat of theatre making. I mentioned that the show is true crime, and it is based on a real Case that happened in the 80s, I was not familiar with the story going in, and I would definitely recommend trying to go in blind if you can. Now, the story is so well told that I don't think even if you go in knowing the full story, it's gonna impact your enjoyment at all. And there's even a sign outside the theatre that literally tells you the full plot. So, like, I don't think they're trying to keep it a surprise. But I do think there's something really novel to experiencing this story for the first time in this medium, because I was just so locked in and constantly excited to find out what was gonna happen next. So if you can go in blind, I think it's worth it. But either way, this is definitely a Broadway Ben must see.
